metadata.title: Redox Biology as an Integrated Network System
metadata.description: The central thesis of this monograph is that cellular redox biology is most faithfully described as an integrated network system whose state variable is a vector of oxidized-to-reduced ratios — NAD⁺/NADH, NADP⁺/NADPH, GSH/GSSG, and TrxSS/TrxSH — resolved by compartment and gated by enzyme kinetics, rather than a scalar index derived from any single couple. Building on a curated synthesis of peer-reviewed primary literature, review articles, and one preprint, the work develops the electrochemical and thermodynamic foundations of this view (Nernstian compartmental potentials; non-equilibrium steady states), formalizes the network as a directed graph of enzymatically gated edges, and examines its central metabolic nodes, glutathione and NAD⁺, together with both pathological directions of stress — oxidative and reductive, the latter mediated by reverse electron transport. Signaling chemistries are treated as network computations: ultrasensitive peroxiredoxin/H₂O₂ kinetics, nuclear sulfenylation, sulfur-based persulfide signaling, and ferroptosis as a redox-dependent cell-fate decision executed by four compartment-mapped removal loops. Physiological integration is traced through circadian–redox feedback loops, immunometabolic reprogramming, and endoplasmic reticulum redox chemistry. Single-cell heterogeneity is shown to place decisive information in distributions rather than means, motivating the genetically encoded biosensor apparatus summarized in tabular form. Finally, the framework's operational requirements — ontology-based model interoperability and redox-aware metabolic engineering, exemplified by the Redox Imbalance Forces Drive strategy achieving 117.65 g/L L-threonine in engineered Escherichia coli — are evaluated. The synthesis positions redox biology as a quantitative, systems-level discipline in which measurement, modeling, and design must jointly respect compartmental insulation, bidirectional stress, and out-of-equilibrium dynamics.
